claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of blood samples from 18 high-responders across three influenza vaccination studies at pre-vaccination and day 7 post-vaccination showed 62 blood transcription modules were significantly altered after vaccination at a Benjamani-Hochberg FDR cutoff of 5%.

sources.quote: To define these response gene sets, QuSAGE meta-analysis was used to compare day 7 post-vaccination with pre-vaccination transcriptional profiles in HR subjects across all three studies. This analysis identified 62 response gene sets with a Benjamani-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff of 5%.
GSE59635 (SDY63) included 7 young subjects (3 LR and 4 HR); GSE59654 (SDY404) contained 13 young subjects (7 LR and 6 HR); GSE59743 (SDY400) had 15 young subjects (7 LR and 8 HR).

comparison.finding: 62 blood transcription modules were significantly altered at day 7 post-vaccination versus pre-vaccination in high-responders across three influenza vaccination studies at a Benjamani-Hochberg FDR cutoff of 5%

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of blood samples from 35 young adults across SDY63, SDY404, and SDY400 at pre-vaccination and day 7 post-vaccination showed 11 gene sets were associated with successful antibody responses, including greater up-regulation of plasma cells, immunoglobulins (M156.1) in high-responders versus low-responders, at a two-sided 15% FDR cutoff.

sources.quote: The goal of the analysis was to detect gene sets associated with successful (i.e., high) antibody responses using the transcriptional response data measured from blood samples taken pre- and 7 days post-vaccination.

As expected from the known biology, "plasma cells, immunoglobulins (M156.1)" was one of top-ranked gene sets from QuSAGE meta-analysis ( Fig 2 ), and was significantly more up-regulated (day 7 vs. pre-vaccination) in HR compared to LR. In total, QuSAGE meta-analysis identified 11 gene sets associated with a successful antibody response ( Table 2 ).
Statistical significance of the meta-analysis was calculated by testing whether the central tendency of the final PDF is zero using a two-sided test with 15% FDR cutoff.
GSE59635 (SDY63) included 7 young subjects (3 LR and 4 HR); GSE59654 (SDY404) contained 13 young subjects (7 LR and 6 HR); GSE59743 (SDY400) had 15 young subjects (7 LR and 8 HR).

comparison.finding: high-responders showed greater up-regulation of plasma cells, immunoglobulins (M156.1) (day 7 vs. pre-vaccination) than low-responders; 11 gene sets were associated with successful antibody responses at a two-sided 15% FDR cutoff

claim_3.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of pre-vaccination and day 28 post-vaccination samples from the three influenza vaccination studies classified subjects as high-responders or low-responders based on adjusted maximum fold change (adjMFC) antibody responses.

sources.quote: Subjects were categorized as high-responders (HR) and low-responders (LR) based on their adjusted maximum fold change (adjMFC) from hemagglutination inhibition assay (HAI) measurements taken pre- and 28 days post-vaccination [ 22 ].

comparison.finding: subjects were classified as high-responders or low-responders based on adjusted maximum fold change (adjMFC) antibody responses from pre-vaccination and day 28 post-vaccination HAI measurements
